response: According to the findings, Chile's traffic law reform did have an impact on police enforcement practices. The reform required changes in police enforcement practices in order to have an effect on reducing traffic fatality and injury rates. This suggests that the traffic law reform did push for police enforcement, as changes in enforcement practices were necessary to achieve the desired outcomes. Additionally, the case highlights the importance of global diffusion of successful road safety practices, promoted by organizations such as the WHO and World Bank, in enhancing national road safety practices.
